title: Every body-supplied gateway secret_id must be authorized through _get_gateway_secret_permission(secret_id) with USE
answers: How do I authorize a secret_id that comes from the request body instead of the URL or query?
Which permission do I need to let a route use a gateway secret?
Why does _get_permission_from_gateway_secret_id read the request param but my validator reads the body?
Should READ or USE be required for a route that decrypts a gateway secret?
body:
Invariant: using a gateway secret for a server-side action (decrypting its key) requires USE on that secret. READ only exposes masked metadata.
Enforced in: mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:_get_gateway_secret_permission(secret_id) takes the id explicitly and returns the role permission or default floor. _get_permission_from_gateway_secret_id() is the thin wrapper that reads secret_id from the request param for the gateway secret RPCs.
Convention: a validator that has already parsed a secret_id from the body must call _get_gateway_secret_permission(secret_id) directly rather than _get_request_param, so the body is read once and the value checked is the one the handler uses.
Breaks if skipped: a route can decrypt a secret the caller only holds READ on, or the body and param values can diverge.
Tests: tests/server/auth/test_auth.py:test_issue_detection_invoke_requires_use_permission_on_secret asserts 403 for UPDATE-only, READ-only and unknown ids, and non-403 with USE or as owner.
applies: Any basic-auth validator or route that accepts a gateway secret_id and makes the server use the secret's key.
says: Users with view only permissions are able to decrypt and use stored gateway credentials.
Running issue detection should require explicit usage permissions on the configured gateway secret.
Deny access when an API request attempts to use credentials with only read privileges.
Access denied error occurs when triggering gateway features without proper secret utilization rights.
search: Basic-auth validators handling a body-supplied secret_id must call mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:_get_gateway_secret_permission(secret_id) and require USE permission to perform server-side key decryption. Validators must pass the parsed body value directly instead of reading request parameters through _get_permission_from_gateway_secret_id to prevent value divergence and unauthorized decryption by callers holding only READ access. As tested in test_issue_detection_invoke_requires_use_permission_on_secret, routes like validate_can_invoke_issue_detection reject READ-only, UPDATE-only, and unknown IDs with a 403 status.
